I get really tired of sensational headlines in regard to science advancement. Aside from the obvious fact that it hurts science by spreading misinformation to those who don't fully read/understand the article, it also serves to undermine the importance of each discovery. I have yet to read an article which fully explains this advancement without mentioning the "wormhole" aspect. By telling the truth without hyperbole, the writer can more fully comment on the importance of the masked pathway which they have created.

For instance, while the magnetic field cannot be detected, does this mean that the effects of the magnetic field will not influence surrounding matter/energy? In an ever growing world of electro-magnetic interference, such a pathway would be insanely useful in electronics as this would allow for cables to transmit information without corruption. An issue which I have previously faced in network planning and implementation has been from magnetic interference in network cables. One particular job which I recall was when I was asked to figure out why WiFi and cables in a store weren't working properly. The WiFi itself didn't seem too be working no matter how many times they replaced/checked the wireless access points and certain cables going through that area had higher rates of data corruption than others. As it turned out, the fluorescent lights were causing the EMI and no-one had thought to check this.This is literally one of the first things they teach you when you study networking but apparently the people in charge of setting up the network had failed to account for the building design. It was a failure in communication between the IT staff of the parent company and the architects who had approved the building design. My solution was to replace those lights as it was not possible to change the building layout or the cable layout.
